steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention
summary: The method replaces RoPE positional embeddings with a composite trainable decay mechanism in a Universal Attention architecture, using the decay values as an adaptive criterion to prune low-contribution tokens from the KV cache during inference. The cost is that the mechanism is end-to-end trained, so it requires pretraining or fine-tuning the model itself rather than being a drop-in inference-time change to existing checkpoints, and it adds architectural complexity. It can fail if decay-based pruning degrades on workloads whose attention patterns differ from the evaluated natural language and synthetic tasks, if quality claims do not transfer to other model families, or if no pretrained checkpoints using this architecture become available for the reader's models.
rationale: Because the technique requires training the architecture end-to-end, which the reader's constrained infrastructure and no-foundation-model-training constraint rule out, it is relevant to track but not adoptable until compatible pretrained models or an inference-only variant exist.
